As of July 2026, India has a total of 52,718 public electric vehicle (EV) charging stations. Among these, 16,561 stations are equipped with fast charging capabilities, providing quicker charging options for EV users [1].

India's public EV charging infrastructure has expanded to include 52,718 stations as of mid-2026. This reflects the country's growing commitment to supporting electric mobility and addressing the charging needs of an increasing number of EVs on the road [1].

Out of the total public charging stations, 16,561 offer fast charging services. Fast chargers are critical for reducing charging time and enhancing the convenience of EV usage, thereby encouraging wider adoption of electric vehicles in India [1].

# Research Report: Outlay and Capacity Target of the PLI Scheme for Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage

The Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) Battery Storage has a total financial outlay of ₹18,100 crore. It aims to promote domestic manufacturing by establishing a cumulative ACC capacity target of 50 GWh in India.

## Financial Outlay and Objectives  
The PLI ACC Scheme is allocated ₹18,100 crore to incentivize and boost the domestic production of advanced chemistry cell batteries. This substantial investment underscores the government's commitment to developing a robust battery manufacturing ecosystem within India. The scheme specifically targets the promotion of advanced, long-range electric vehicle (EV) batteries, linking incentives to sales performance to encourage market-driven growth.

## Capacity Target  
A key goal of the PLI ACC Scheme is to establish a cumulative manufacturing capacity of 50 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of advanced chemistry cell batteries in India. This capacity target is designed to meet the growing demand for EV batteries and support the country's transition to cleaner transportation technologies.

## Implementation Timeline  
The performance phase of the scheme is scheduled from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2029. This five-year period will be critical for achieving the capacity and production targets set under the scheme.

# Research Report: Growth Projections for India's EV Market and EV Battery Market

India's electric vehicle (EV) market has experienced exponential growth, expanding approximately 46 times from 50,000 units sold in 2016 to 2.3 million units projected in 2025. Concurrently, the EV battery manufacturing ecosystem in India is rapidly developing, driven by significant investments from domestic OEMs and global battery manufacturers aiming to establish large-scale production facilities.

## Growth of India's EV Market

India's EV market has witnessed remarkable expansion over the past decade, with sales increasing from about 50,000 units in 2016 to an anticipated 2.3 million units in 2025, representing a growth factor of approximately 46 times [1][2][3][6][7]. This growth rate significantly outpaces the global EV sales growth, which rose about 20 times from 918,000 units in 2016 to 18.78 million units in 2024 [1][3][6][7]. The compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of EV registrations in India has exceeded 62% over the last ten years [1][3][4][6][7].

The adoption rate of EVs in India has also surged, increasing from a mere 0.08% in fiscal year 2015-16 to an estimated 8.26% in fiscal year 2025-26 [1][3][4][6][7]. This reflects a growing consumer acceptance and supportive policy environment.

### Segment-wise Contributions

By fiscal year 2025, electric two-wheelers are projected to dominate the Indian EV market with sales of approximately 1.28 million units [1][3][6][7]. Electric three-wheelers also contribute significantly, with sales expected to reach 800,000 units in the same period [1][3][6][7]. These segments have been pivotal in driving the overall market expansion.

### Export Growth

India's EV exports have similarly expanded, rising from USD 1.2 million in 2020 to USD 84 million in 2024, indicating growing international demand and competitiveness of Indian EV products [1][2][3][4][6][7].

## Development of India's EV Battery Market

The EV battery manufacturing ecosystem in India is undergoing rapid expansion, supported by substantial investments in research and development, gigafactory construction, and dedicated EV platforms by leading Indian original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) such as Tata Motors, Mahindra, TVS, and Bajaj Auto [1][3][4][5][7]. This domestic push aims to enhance localization and reduce costs.

In addition to domestic players, global companies including VinFast, Tesla, and prominent Korean and Japanese battery manufacturers are exploring large-scale EV battery production in India [4][5][7]. Their entry is expected to strengthen the local supply chain, improve technology transfer, and boost cost competitiveness in the Indian EV battery market.

## What We Could Not Establish

The available data does not provide explicit quantitative projections for the size or growth rate of India's EV battery market in terms of production capacity, revenue, or market share. While the ecosystem's expansion and investments are noted, specific growth metrics for the battery segment remain unspecified.

# Allocation for Electric Buses under the PM E-DRIVE Scheme

The PM E-DRIVE scheme has allocated ₹4,391 crore for the procurement of 14,028 electric buses. Of these, 13,800 buses are designated for deployment across seven major cities, with procurement processes underway in phased stages.

## Financial Allocation and Bus Quantity

The total budget allocated under the PM E-DRIVE scheme for electric buses stands at ₹4,391 crore, which covers the procurement of 14,028 electric buses [1] [2] [3] [4] [6] [8] [11] [14] [15] [16]. This allocation reflects a significant investment in electrifying public transport fleets across India.

## Distribution Across Cities

Out of the total 14,028 buses, 13,800 have been allocated to seven major cities: Bengaluru, Delhi, Mumbai, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Pune, and Surat [2] [7] [14] [15] [16]. This distribution highlights a focus on urban centers with high public transport demand.

## Procurement Phases

The procurement process is divided into two phases. Phase I has concluded with the procurement of 10,900 electric buses, while tenders for the remaining 2,900 buses under Phase II were floated in early 2026 [2] [5] [7] [14] [15] [16]. This phased approach facilitates systematic deployment and scaling.

- Switch Mobility secured an order to supply 840 electric buses for Delhi under Phase I, comprising equal numbers of nine-metre and twelve-metre air-conditioned buses (420 each) [9] [10] [13].
- Delhi has approved the procurement of 2,800 electric buses under the scheme, split evenly between nine-metre and twelve-metre buses (1,400 each) [12] [14] [15] [16].

# Research Report: India Electric Mobility Index

The India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) is a pioneering framework launched by NITI Aayog in August 2025 to monitor and compare the progress of Indian States and Union Territories in electric mobility. It ranks regions based on their ecosystem strength, with Delhi, Maharashtra, and Chandigarh identified as the highest-ranking Frontrunners.

## Overview of the India Electric Mobility Index

The IEMI serves as a comprehensive tool to evaluate the advancement of electric mobility across India. It assesses performance using 16 indicators organized into three key pillars:

- **Transport Electrification:** Measures the adoption and penetration of electric vehicles.
- **Charging Infrastructure Readiness:** Evaluates the availability and accessibility of EV charging stations.
- **EV Research & Innovation:** Assesses the region's efforts in developing new technologies and innovations in electric mobility.

This multi-dimensional approach provides a clear snapshot of each region's electric mobility ecosystem strength, enabling targeted policy interventions and benchmarking.

## Classification of Regions

Based on their IEMI scores, States and Union Territories are categorized into three groups:

- **Frontrunners:** Regions with robust and mature electric mobility ecosystems.
- **Performers:** Regions showing steady progress in developing their EV infrastructure and adoption.
- **Aspirants:** Regions that require significant intervention to improve their electric mobility landscape.

## Top-Ranked Regions

According to the latest IEMI results, Delhi, Maharashtra, and Chandigarh have emerged as Frontrunners. These regions demonstrate strong and mature electric vehicle ecosystems, reflecting their leadership in transport electrification, infrastructure readiness, and innovation.

# India's Dependence on Imported Lithium: A 2026 Overview

India remains entirely dependent on imported lithium as of 2026, with no significant domestic production or refining capacity. This reliance, particularly on finished lithium-ion battery cells from China, presents strategic challenges that the government is actively addressing through incentives, international partnerships, and recycling initiatives.

## Complete Import Dependence

India is 100% import-dependent for lithium in 2026 [5] [6] [7] [9] [10]. Domestic lithium production is negligible, limited to preliminary surveys indicating 1,600 tonnes of inferred lithium resources in Karnataka, which is insignificant compared to demand [6]. Although lithium reserves of 5.9 million tons were discovered in Jammu and Kashmir in 2023, extraction has stalled due to low lithium concentration, difficult clay deposits, and security concerns in the disputed region [1] [2] [3]. Furthermore, India currently has effectively zero lithium refining capacity, making it reliant on imports not only for raw lithium but also for refined lithium products [4].

## Import Composition and Sources

India’s lithium imports are dominated by finished lithium-ion battery cells and packs, which accounted for 84.32% of the lithium import value in Q1 2026 [5]. These finished products primarily come from China, which is the largest supplier, followed by Vietnam, Japan, South Korea, and the United States [5] [6]. Imports include lithium-ion accumulators (finished cells and packs), battery parts, and lithium compounds, with the majority being finished lithium-ion batteries [5] [6].

## Economic Impact and Strategic Vulnerability

India’s lithium import bill surged to $4.7 billion in 2025, nearly nine times the 2018 figure, reflecting rapidly growing demand for lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles and energy storage [7]. This heavy dependence on imports, especially from China, poses a strategic vulnerability for India’s electric vehicle and energy storage sectors [4] [8] [9] [10].

## Government Initiatives and Future Outlook

To reduce import dependence, the Indian government has launched a Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme with an outlay of Rs. 18,100 crore (~$2.16 billion) aimed at promoting domestic manufacturing of advanced chemistry cell (ACC) batteries [6] [4] [12] [13]. India is also pursuing international partnerships and investments to secure lithium supply, including exploration rights in Argentina and Australia, though production from these sources is expected only after several years [8] [11]. Additionally, India is promoting lithium battery recycling (urban mining) as a domestic source to mitigate import reliance [7].

## What We Could Not Establish

There are no significant gaps in the available information regarding India’s lithium import dependence as of 2026.

# Research Report: CO2 Targets in Upcoming CAFE Norms for India

The upcoming CAFE III norms for light-duty vehicles in India set a WLTP-based CO2 emission target of 91.7 grams per kilometer for 2027 to 2032. Subsequently, the CAFE IV norms planned for 2033 to 2037 aim to tighten this target further to 70 grams per kilometer, also based on WLTP standards.

## CAFE III Norms (2027-2032)

The CAFE III standards propose a WLTP CO2 emission target of 91.7 g/km for light-duty vehicles. To aid original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) in meeting these targets, a super-credit mechanism will be introduced. This mechanism incentivizes increased sales of electric vehicles, allowing OEMs to offset emissions from conventional vehicles and thus facilitate compliance [1] [2] [3].

## CAFE IV Norms (2033-2037)

Following the CAFE III phase, India plans to implement CAFE IV norms with a more stringent CO2 emission target of 70 g/km, also measured using the WLTP procedure. This reflects a continued commitment to reducing vehicular emissions and promoting cleaner transportation technologies [2] [3].
